text_plugin_synopsis: JavaScript libraries and Node compatibility shims for require in AutoJs6 scripts
p_languages_all_supported_for_readme: The README.md file is currently available in the following languages
p_introduction_what: Bundled Libraries holds the {{ library_count }} script libraries that used to be built into AutoJs6: axios, cheerio, dayjs, i18n, pangu and lodash, plus the Node compatibility shims buffer, events, fs, os, path, process and nodejs. Starting with AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }}, the AutoJs6 package no longer includes them; with this plugin installed and enabled, `require('axios')`, `require('fs')` and the like, as well as the global objects `axios`, `cheerio`, `dayjs`, `i18n` and `pangu`, keep working exactly as before.
p_introduction_how: The plugin is only a resource package: AutoJs6 reads the library files straight from the plugin package, scripts never start the plugin process, and the plugin needs no storage, network or other permission (the network requests of axios are made by AutoJs6, which runs the script). Libraries you do not need can be switched off one by one on the plugin page.
p_libraries_intro: The module names are the arguments of `require`; a library with a global object can also be used without `require`. Sources and licenses of the libraries are listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md]({{ notices_url }}).
usage_steps: Use AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} ({{ required_host_version_code }}) or later.
Install Bundled Libraries from the Plugin Center of AutoJs6 (or download the APK from [Releases]({{ repo_url }}/releases)) and make sure the plugin is enabled.

p_usage_note: There is a single universal package without native libraries, for devices with Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) or later.
p_switches_intro: The plugin page (opened from the Plugin Center of AutoJs6 or the Bundled Libraries icon on the home screen) has one switch per library, all on by default
switch_points: A library that is switched off can no longer be required and its global object cannot be used; switch it on again to restore it.
A switch applies to the next `require`: modules that a running script has already loaded stay until the script ends.
`fs` needs `buffer`, and `nodejs` needs `process` and `buffer`: with `buffer` or `process` switched off, the modules that need them cannot load either.
"Release history" at the bottom of the page lists the changes of each version.
p_unavailable_intro: When the plugin is not installed, not authorized, disabled in the Plugin Center or incompatible, or a library is switched off, `require` of that library and reading its global object throw an error
unavailable_points: The error is an `Error` with `code` `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; its message says whether to install the plugin or where to switch it on, and scripts can handle it with `try...catch`.
The error object also has `library` (the library name) and `reason` (`not-installed`, `unauthorized`, `plugin-disabled`, `library-disabled` or `incompatible`).
A change of the plugin state never interrupts a running script, it only affects later `require` calls; the other built-in modules of AutoJs6 and the script's own files are not affected.
compatibility_points: Requires AutoJs6 {{ required_host_version_name }} (build {{ required_host_version_code }}) or later; earlier versions of AutoJs6 include these libraries themselves and do not need the plugin.
Supports Android {{ min_android_version }} (API {{ android_min_sdk }}) or later, one package for all processor architectures.
The library files are identical to the ones that used to be built into AutoJs6, so existing scripts need no change.
The plugin serves the default JavaScript scripts of AutoJs6; scripts of the Node.js runtime plugin use the modules of Node.js itself.

faq.q: Why does AutoJs6 no longer include these libraries?
faq.a: Only some scripts use them. As a plugin they keep the AutoJs6 package smaller, whoever needs them installs the plugin, and only the libraries in use need to stay on. The files in the plugin are the same as the built-in ones.

faq.q: My script uses the global object `axios` directly. Do I have to switch to `require`?
faq.a: No. The global objects `axios`, `cheerio`, `dayjs`, `i18n` and `pangu` are the same modules that `require` returns, and both load them from this plugin.

faq.q: Does the plugin go online or run in the background?
faq.a: No. The plugin has no network permission, and running a script never starts the plugin process. The network requests of axios are made by AutoJs6, which runs the script.

faq.q: The error says the plugin needs to be authorized. What should I do?
faq.a: The release from the Plugin Center of AutoJs6 or from the Releases of this project needs no authorization. A build of your own has a different signature and must first be authorized in the Plugin Center as prompted.
